THE STAR
(With dedication to U Soso Tham)
Youth, behold before thy face,
Know which way yoor steps to aim.
There s a Star your path to trace.
For living name and lasting fame.
Bxert yourself, then, like a man;
Work not just to feed your frame.
Upward so your life to span.
To the height of living fame.

Not to gather riches vast,
Nor wide boundaries thus to claim.
For these things can never last
As a name and lasting fame.
For your weakness though you grieve,
Powerless, yet always game ;
Who can t say you won t achieve-
Living name and lasting fame.
Fear not, then to forge ahead.
Through the sword and through the flame;

A CRITICAL APPREOATION
I have read with absorbing interest the poem endtled
KA JITLAKHAl composed by E. Weston Dkhat. The
poem centres round the life of a certain qneen JitialAai to
name of War Shelia mythology in the southern part of Kfaimi
Hills who lived long enough to rule for one hundred and
fifty years at least symbolically. The queen is endowed
with all the qualities of head and heart. She is said to
possess rare toauty. In short, Jitlakhai represents the best and
the noblest ingrained in the Golden age. In course of time
due to greed, avarice and pride man succumbs to the evil
forces of life. The Golden age comes to an abrupt end,
and its place is usurped by a demoniac age. The poet sym

bolises this change or transition from a golden age into a
demoniac age through two characters who are the ministars
of the queen. Myrmiet is on the side of justice and
righteousness while Shynrit represents all the disruptive
forces of life. There is a perpetual war between the two
something like dualism found in some religions, and in the
end the forces of evil triumph over the forces of good. The
queen is changed into a stone, and one of the ministers
U Myrmiet dies of a broken art. The Queen s father
U Thu Kunok dies in a similar fashion. All the good
things of life disintegrate — complete negation of all the
accepted values.
The poet mourns over the passing away of the Golden
age as the demoniac age emerges and makes its appearance
on the scene. He does not however lose hope for beyond
the horizons man will be finally liberated from, the
shackles of life. There will be an ushering in of a new ma
where justice and righteousness will once again return.
Where justice will roll down like waters, and righteouineea
like an ever flowing stream .
